approach: backfill the whole clibuilder surface as its own mission, chosen by the Council over a scoped root-plus-touched-nodes cut
capability-first layout, ten nodes, colocated per the args-minus precedent
partition-quality measured and declined to decide; layout follows the recommendation, not the numbers
the zod removal that prompted this is deferred to a later mission

summary: replace zod with Standard Schema for configuration plus an in-house type descriptor for arguments and options, and stop re-exporting z from the public entry point
why: the framework pins every consumer to its own validator major, and the validator is its heaviest runtime dependency on a package that optimizes startup

summary: an option's `default` is not type-checked against its declared `type`
why: cli.Command.Options is Record<Name, Options.Entry<Type>> with Type defaulting to z.ZodType<any> and never inferred per entry, so Entry's `default?: z.infer<Type>` widens to any. `{ type: z.array(z.string()), default: 5 }` compiles and the option still types as string[], so run receives a value its own declaration says is impossible. Closing it needs per-entry inference of Type; verified against ts/cli.ts during the command-definition backfill.

summary: the `--` terminator remainder never reaches the run arguments, and using `--` emits a spurious invalid-key error
why: fillInputOptions skips the `_` key but not `__`, so `__` falls through to lookupOptions, matches no declared option, and pushes {type:'invalid-key',key:'__'}. lookupCommand.Result declares an `__?: string[]` field that is therefore unreachable. Verified: parseArgv(['node','cli','--','abc']) yields {_:[],__:['abc']}, and lookupCommand on a command with no options returns errors [{invalid-key,__}] and args {_:[]}.

summary: `--` arriving while an option awaits values is consumed as that option's value instead of opening the terminator
why: isOption('--') is false (no word character), so the reducer's option-state branch claims the token before the `v === '--'` branch is reached. Verified: parseArgv(['node','cli','--opt','--','abc']) yields {_:[],opt:['--','abc']} with no __ at all.

summary: a negative number on the command line is tokenized as an option
why: isOption('-5') is true because the token starts with '-' and /\w+/ matches its digits, so startSingleCharacterOptions opens an option named '5'. A command declaring a number argument or option cannot be given a negative value. Verified: parseArgv(['node','cli','-5']) yields {'5':['true'],_:[]}.

summary: the display level cannot be set back to info once raised
why: createUI's displayLevel setter switches on none, debug, and trace only, with no case for 'info', so assigning 'info' is a silent no-op. Benign today because createUI constructs the logger at info, so the initial value is already correct; it means a caller that raised the level to debug or trace has no way to lower it back.

summary: mockPluginContext.register discards the Registration result, so a refused registration is silent in tests
why: the real activation context in plugins.ts inspects the result and warns when a key is already owned by another source. ts/testing/mock_plugin_context.ts calls registry.register(source, key, value) and ignores the return, so a plugin colliding with another plugin's key passes its own tests silently and only warns in production — exactly the case the test double exists to catch.

summary: mockContext.resolveConfig does not cache, unlike the real context
why: context.ts caches the resolution as a promise so concurrent callers share one filesystem walk and a falsy config is not re-resolved. context.mock.ts calls resolveConfig afresh on every invocation, so no test observes the caching and a regression removing it from production would not be caught.

summary: three nodes exceed the 40-scenario soft ceiling and may want splitting
why: check-spec-structure reports oversized-node advisories: execution 48, input-parsing 48, presentation 45. Each is a breadth profile (6, 5, and 6 use-case clusters respectively) rather than depth, so the split would be along use-case lines — e.g. presentation's help generation apart from its collection rendering. Advisory only, and a formation (Warden) call rather than this backfill's; the layout this mission committed to is ten nodes.

summary: a plugin package that cannot be imported is warned about twice, once as unloadable and once as not a valid plugin
why: loadModule returns undefined on a failed import, and isValidPlugin(undefined) is false, so the same plugin takes the `no` branch of both decisions; the second warning tells the user their package is malformed when the real fault was the import

summary: `ts/render/error.ts` is governed by execution/ but sits among presentation/'s files
why: the ts/ refactor split errors.ts into error data (app/errors.ts) and error text (render/error.ts). The text half implements execution/'s UC3 usage-error descriptions, so behaviour puts it in execution/ while the folder puts it beside presentation/'s renderers. Re-partitioning would move 8 scenarios between two frozen-candidate suites, which is a Warden call at the formation loop rather than a path update — recorded here so the next formation pass decides it deliberately

supersedes: `ts/render/error.ts` is governed by execution/ but sits among presentation/'s files
summary: execution/'s UC3 usage-error scenarios belong to presentation/; the stated reason for keeping them is factually wrong
why: the earlier entry framed this as a judgement call between two defensible homes. It is not. presentation/'s non-goals say "Describing a usage error in words belongs to execution/, which owns the error types" - but execution/ does not own them. `lookupCommand.Error` is declared in ts/invocation/lookup.ts and input-parsing/'s surface trace claims it ("lookupCommand.Result.errors and its five error types | UC2"). execution/ only calls the formatter. The code is presentation throughout: five returns producing strings plus two formatting helpers. So the 8 scenarios under execution/'s UC3 usage-error section should move to presentation/, and presentation/'s non-goal sentence should be deleted rather than reworded. Left for the Warden because it moves scenarios between two suites about to be frozen - but it is a correction, not a preference

summary: `lookupCommand.ExpectSingle.value` is typed `any` when every producer passes `string[]`
why: all four construction sites (ts/invocation/lookup.ts:207,211,215,246) push `value: values`, which is always a string[]. The loose type forced defensive code downstream: `toArray()` in ts/render/error.ts exists only to handle a scalar that production never produces, and the sole caller passing one is the test written to cover that branch (ts/render/error.spec.ts:50). Narrowing `value` to `string[]` makes `toArray` dead and removes both. Deferred rather than done now: the suite fixes 'too many values are described with the values that were given' as current behaviour, so tightening the type before the gate would narrow a frozen-candidate scenario's shape and should fire Clearance rather than slip in ahead of it

summary: formatKey's argument branch is unreachable for an expect-single error
why: ts/render/error.ts:22 renders expect-single through formatKey, which branches on whether the key is a declared argument. It never can be: ts/invocation/lookup.ts:89 gives a non-array argument exactly one value ([args.shift()]), so values.length > 1 never holds for it, and an array argument takes the array branch of toParsable, which never pushes expect-single. Only a repeated option reaches it. The argument half of that branch is dead on this path while staying live for invalid-value, which shares formatKey. Specified as-is: the spec now states expect-single always names an option. Related to entry 14 (ExpectSingle.value typed any keeping toArray alive) — the same loose typing hides both.

summary: test-utils/argv silently splits an argument containing a space
why: argv(input) is `node ${input}`.split(' '), so an argument containing a space becomes two arguments with no signal to the caller. A command author testing a space-bearing argument gets a wrong argv and a confusing failure. Now specified as current behavior with its own scenario; a future CR should consider whether the helper should refuse or quote instead. Raised by the testing/ spec-judge at the re-judge.

summary: plugin discovery does not work under Yarn PnP
why: findByKeywords scans node_modules, so `plugins list` reports nothing in a PnP install even though loading and running plugins under PnP works. Recovered from issue #575 (split from #327) during the backfill's unserved-use-case pass, not from the source. Unserved: no entry point exists, so it is recorded as a goal rather than specified.

summary: a TypeScript config file is not supported
why: getConfigFilenames offers .cjs .mjs .js .json .jsonc .yml .yaml and no .ts, so a CLI author cannot write the config in TypeScript. Recovered from issue #405, which suggests sucrase. Unserved.

summary: a plugin cannot update the config file, and is not a listed actor
why: Issue #488 asks for an api to lookup and load config so plugins can read AND update it. The reading half is served and publicly exported; nothing writes a config back. The request also names an actor the node did not list - a plugin - which is the missing-actor half of the same finding. Recovered from the tracker.

summary: a command name or alias colliding with an existing one is not detected
why: Issue #109 asked for a warning on conflict with first-match-wins execution. It was closed without an implementation: no conflict detection exists in ts/app/ or ts/invocation/. Recovered from the tracker; unserved, so recorded as a goal rather than specified.

summary: the backfill's unserved-use-case recovery was skipped for every node until three judge rounds had already run
why: spec-format-governance requires a backfill to recover unserved use cases from request history and the issue tracker, since source yields only served ones by construction, and to record where each came from. No session did this; the omission survived three rounds because the Oracle lens passed 8/8 without testing the clause. Four unserved goals were recovered on the eventual pass (#575, #405, #488, #109). Run this pass before the first gate, not after.

summary: an option declaring a default still types as possibly undefined
why: RunArgs types a declared option as z.infer<OT>, so an optional type stays T | undefined even when a default guarantees a value at runtime. Issue #274 asked for exactly this and was closed without an implementation, the same shape as #109. Verified with a type probe: assigning a defaulted optional-string option to a string errors. Recovered by a targeted parsing-and-typing sweep of the tracker, prompted by the input-parsing judge observing that the first recovery pass left no node-specific audit trail for the highest-complaint area.

summary: gh issue list --search returns nothing in this environment; grep the full list instead
why: The targeted tracker sweep initially came back empty for every keyword. The --search flag silently returns no rows here (it did the same against a second repo), rather than there being no matches. Pulling --limit 100 --json and filtering locally found 13 parsing-relevant issues, one of which was a real unserved goal. Any future recovery pass must not treat an empty --search as evidence of absence.

summary: targeted tracker sweep for testing/ found no unserved goals — recorded so the absence is evidenced
why: The testing/ spec-judge passed the node but noted its missing Unserved-goals table rested on the general pass rather than a domain-specific search, and asked for one before the absence was trusted. Ran it with the local-filter method (gh issue list --search is unreliable here): terms test/mock/fixture/harness/spec/assert/stub/double over the full list returned two issues, #264 and #324. Both target an API generation that no longer exists — createPluginCliTest, createCommand<Config,Context>, onInvoke — and their substance is served by the current testCommand and mockPluginContext: a default command is testable by passing it to testCommand, and the plugin activation context has a mock. Zero unserved goals for this node is therefore a searched result, not an unexamined one.

summary: UC5's Extensions prose narrates config caching but not its plugin-loading twin
why: Sub-graph E draws both LPG/LCACHE (plugin activation caching) and RC2/CACHE (config resolution caching); both have scenario-map rows and scenarios, but only the config half is narrated in UC5's Extensions prose. The same shape as the UC2 gap closed in dc843e6. The judge that found it explicitly declined to fail a lens on it, citing this CR's own precedent that a prose-completeness asymmetry with full scenario coverage is an observation rather than a defect. Recorded rather than fixed: each such fix stales a node's verdict and buys another judge round, and the ledger is never frozen so this survives the freeze.
